Capture works from an address. The server opens the page picked in the design bar in a headless browser and takes the picture there. A modal opened inside the frame never changes any address, so Capture can't see it. It's the same gap that makes Capture miss a page you got to by following a link inside the frame.

**What I recommend:** the framed page reports where it is. Koda already records the address each region's content came from, including the drawer and modal regions. The design's server would add a small script to pages it shows in the frame (it already marks those pages for the client you pick). The script tells the design page the frame's current address and any open overlay's address. Capture then uses the overlay's own address. That address shows the overlay on top of its page, the way Prelude already shows overlays in the preview, so the picture includes the Mark up modal. App mode works the same way, as long as the app shows overlays at their own address too.

**The catch:** Capture loads that address fresh, so anything typed or drawn that hasn't been saved is missing. In your case you'd get the Mark up modal with an empty canvas. To capture exactly what's on screen, there are two options:
- **The desktop app takes the picture itself:** works only in the desktop app.
- **The browser's screen-share prompt:** you'd have to pick the window each time.

Should I design it the recommended way, with a rule that Capture shows where you are (followed links and open drawers or modals)? Or do you need what's typed and drawn in the picture too? The fix itself is in Prelude's server and the design page's views. I'd record it in this design for the build to carry over, plus the rule and a note in NOTES.md.

1984	The host composes. Refusing a panel the address bar says nothing about where
1985	that panel is; the host is free to write it into *its own* URL, and then
1986	`/hub?expenses=/expenses/claims/4023` is a page the host can answer, one back
1987	button still means one thing, and the link survives being pasted.
1988	
1989	That is a host pattern rather than a feature: it needs no attribute and no
1990	option, because every part of it is already published. `koda:attached` announces
1991	each arrival with its region, its element, its URL and its reason; `ko-location`
1992	is where a region is; `go` puts one somewhere; and `history.pushState` is the
1993	browser's. `tools/hub.js` is a worked example. A private back-and-forward stack per
1994	panel (`ko-history="local"`, below) is the answer only where there is no
1995	address bar to compose into.

Capture is now designed to work both ways. In the desktop app it gets the Mark up modal with your drawing; in a browser it gets the modal fresh, without the drawing. I haven't seen it rendered in the preview yet. Nothing in the app has changed until it's built.

- **In a browser:** the page in the frame tells the design page where it is, including any drawer or modal open on top or a page you reached by following links. Capture opens that address afresh, so in your case you'd get the Mark up modal, but with an empty canvas. Anything typed or drawn and not yet saved is missing.
- **In the desktop app:** "What's in view" is the app's own picture of the frame, exactly as it is on screen, including what's typed or drawn. It closes the Capture menu first so the menu isn't in the picture. At a fixed size it keeps the full resolution even though the frame is shown smaller to fit.
- **"The whole page":** opened afresh in both, since the screen never shows all of it at once.
- **App mode:** in a browser it still captures the page picked in the bar, because Prelude can't add the reporting script to the app's own pages. The desktop app's "What's in view" is unaffected.

The Capture menu's hints now say which of these you'll get. To see the desktop wording in the preview, set the client to Desktop app.

To change the menu, I brought the design page's views back into the design. Only `_surface.eta` and `_design-bar.eta` actually changed; the other views are unchanged copies. The work in the app is written up in `NOTES.md`: the reporting script, the server opening the new address, and the desktop shell's screenshot.

Other changes:
- **Rules:** R-k7c is retired, since it only ever pictured the page picked. Two new proposed rules replace it: R-w8p (Capture shows where you are) and R-3qz (what each client includes).
- **App shell:** I added a small rule so something can be hidden in the desktop app (`[data-browser-only]`), the counterpart of the existing desktop-only one. It's noted in the shell's `NOTES.md`.

The preview can't show this one correctly yet, and I can't change that from inside the design.

The rule that hides the browser's hint in the desktop app (`[data-browser-only]`) is in the shell's CSS. But the preview loads the app's own copy of that CSS, `server/public/shell.css`, because the shell's layouts were ported to the app. That copy doesn't have the new rule yet, and it's an app file I can't edit. So with Desktop app picked, the preview shows both hints. With Browser picked it shows only the browser's hint, which is correct. Once built, the app's copy is replaced with the shell's version and only one hint shows.

I briefly put a copy of the rule in the design's `styles.css`, then took it out: the app's layout doesn't load that file either. I've noted the limitation in `NOTES.md`.

If you'd like to check the desktop wording now, I can put the rule in the design system's CSS instead, since the preview loads that file live. I'd rather not: it belongs to the shell, and it would be a second copy someone has to remove later.
